notes.decision: Translated 'to reckon them.' Analyzed as ⲁ-ⲧ(ⲣⲉ-)ⲟⲩ-ⲟⲩⲱⲡ-ⲟⲩ 'to make them count' or causative-purpose construction on ⲱⲡ 'count, reckon' (in glossary), with prosthetic ⲟⲩ- and Lyc. vowel-split ⲱ → ⲟ̄ⲁ. The same form recurs as ⲛ̄ⲥⲉⲟ̄ⲁⲡⲟⲩ (l.12) and ⲥⲉⲟ̄ⲁⲡⲟⲩ (l.23) confirming 3pl object suffix on a reckoning-verb.

Translated as a doublet 'flight and dispersal' — ⲡⲱⲧ 'flee' (verbal noun) + ⲛ̄ⲥⲱⲣ 'and scattering' (cf. glossary ⲡⲣⲉϩⲥⲱⲩⲥ 'gatherer' inversely). The phrase opens by referencing topics from end of previous page.

Translated 'shall be raised up' — relative future on ϫⲓⲥⲉ 'raise, be high' with 3sg.f object. Same root underlies ⲡⲭⲥⲉ 'the Height' (in glossary). Note this is distinct from the soteriological ⲧⲟⲩⲱ 'raise.'

Translated 'the gloom of wind.' ⲛⲟⲫⲟⲥ < Greek γνόφος/κνέφας 'gloom, gathering darkness.' The dark-wind/gloomy-wind is the first of three Virgin-of-Light signs catalogued in this chapter, paired with vehemence/harshness.
Translated 'gusts.' Lexeme uncertain; likely Lyc. plural for 'wind-gusts, blasts' paired with ⲛⲓⲧⲏⲩ 'winds.' Could alternatively be 'storms' or 'breezes.' Confidence moderate.
Translated 'they habitually make waves.' Habitual ϣⲁⲩ- + ⲣ̄- + ⲍⲁⲓⲙⲉ from ϩⲟⲉⲓⲙ/ⲍⲓⲙⲉⲩⲉ 'wave' (in glossary). The cloud-and-wind, descending into rivers and seas, agitates them.
Translated 'their ships.' Lyc. ⲝⲏⲩ likely = ϫⲏⲩ 'ships' (per glossary entry ⲛⲉⲭⲏⲩ for cosmic light-vessels). Fits the maritime sequence: rivers/seas → waves → ships → fish.

Translated 'one habitually finds her gathered.' ϣⲁⲕ-ⲟ̄ⲛⲧ-ⲥ as Lyc. habitual+verb+3sg.f, possibly from ϭⲛ̄ 'find.' ⲉⲥ-ⲥⲟ̄ⲏⲣ circumstantial 'while she is gathered/at rest.' The Virgin-sign is one of stillness and quiet.
Translated 'quietness.' Lexeme paired here twice with ⲟⲩⲍⲣⲁⲕ 'stillness' as a cosmic-quietude doublet. Likely related to ϭⲁⲙⲏ/ϫⲁⲙⲏ 'tranquility, calm.' Confidence moderate.

Translated 'the cloud also which habitually departs upward.' Note that ⲭⲉⲥⲧ in glossary is 'depart upward / be raised up,' confirming the editor's restoration of ⲁⲍⲣⲏⲓ̈ 'upward' at the end of this line.

Tentatively translated 'an unutterable thing of them.' Analyzed as ⲛ̄ⲟⲩ- (indefinite art.) + ⲁⲧ- (privative) + ⲟⲩⲱ ('utter, declare') + ⲟⲩ (3pl) = 'an undeclared/unutterable (thing) of them.' Could alternatively be 'innumerable.' Confidence low.
